claim: The Tailscale status JSON's Status.BackendState field takes exactly the documented string values NoState, NeedsLogin, NeedsMachineAuth, Stopped, Starting, Running.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should model tailscale connectivity as a small enumerated state machine via BackendState rather than binary up/down
scope_conditions: tailscale.com/ipn/ipnstate package, module v1.102.3 (Aug 2026); applies to all 'tailscale status --json' consumers
quoted_support: BackendState is an ipn.State string value: "NoState", "NeedsLogin", "NeedsMachineAuth", "Stopped", "Starting", "Running".

claim: Tailscale Status JSON exposes a Health field that is a list of health-check problem strings, where an empty list means no known problems detected — a ready-made machine-readable health sensor for a fleet agent.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can surface tailscale daemon health directly from status JSON without inventing its own heuristics
scope_conditions: tailscale.com/ipn/ipnstate Status struct; consumed via tailscale status --json

claim: PeerStatus.Online means connected to the Tailscale control plane, while PeerStatus.Active means some packet was sent to the peer in the past two minutes — two distinct liveness signals with explicitly unstable semantics.
stance_target: a fleet agent monitoring peer reachability must distinguish control-plane Online from data-plane Active, and must not hard-code the Active definition
scope_conditions: ipnstate PeerStatus struct; Active definition documented as subject to change

claim: PeerStatus carries per-peer traffic counters (RxBytes, TxBytes int64), timing data (LastWrite, LastSeen, LastHandshake), the DERP Relay region, and the current direct address CurAddr — sufficient raw material for per-peer link-quality sensors in an agent.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can build per-host network telemetry from tailscale status --json without shelling out to additional tools
scope_conditions: ipnstate PeerStatus fields as of v1.102.3
quoted_support:
RxBytes        int64
TxBytes        int64
Created        time.Time // time registered with tailcontrol
LastWrite      time.Time // time last packet sent
LastSeen       time.Time // last seen to tailcontrol; only present if offline
LastHandshake  time.Time // with local wireguard

claim: The ipnstate PeerStatus struct is internally merged by StatusBuilder.AddPeer, and the source carries a warning that adding new fields without updating AddPeer may lead to inconsistencies or lost data — signalling that even Tailscale treats this status surface as evolving.
stance_target: agents parsing tailscale status --json must pin a tailscale version and tolerate schema drift, because the schema is internally versioned and merged
quoted_support: WARNING: The fields in PeerStatus are merged by the AddPeer method in the StatusBuilder. When adding a new field to PeerStatus, you must update AddPeer to handle merging the new field.

claim: ExitNodeStatus (added v1.28.0) reports the current exit node's StableNodeID, Online bool, and TailscaleIPs, and PeerStatus.ExitNodeOption distinguishes nodes that are offered-and-approved exit nodes from the currently selected ExitNode.
stance_target: an agent can report which exit node a jupiterOS host uses and whether it is alive, straight from status JSON

claim: PeerStatus.IsRouter() (added v1.102.0) identifies nodes that route addresses besides their own — exit nodes, subnet routers, app connectors — giving an agent a first-class way to classify routing nodes in the tailnet.
stance_target: fleet topology sensing: an agent can enumerate which jupiterOS hosts act as subnet routers or exit nodes
quoted_support:
IsRouter reports whether ps describes a router:
a node that routes addresses besides its own.
Examples: an exit node, a subnet router, an app connector, etc.

claim: tailscale ping results are structured as PingResult with LatencySeconds, the direct Endpoint used, the DERP region ID/code when relayed, and Err — so latency probing a fleet can be done via the CLI in JSON-adjacent structured form rather than parsing ping text.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent inter-host latency sensing via tailscale ping without text parsing
scope_conditions: ipnstate PingResult; surfaced by tailscale ping command
quoted_support:
type PingResult struct {
IP       string // ping destination
NodeIP   string // Tailscale IP of node handling IP (different for subnet routers)
NodeName string // DNS name base or (possibly not unique) hostname

Err            string
LatencySeconds float64

claim: The tailnet lock state is inspectable via TailnetLockStatus (Enabled, NodeKeySigned, TrustedKeys, FilteredPeers for nodes removed from the netmap for failing lock checks), which matters for fleet agents because lock-filtered peers silently lose connectivity.
stance_target: agent reliability: a jupiterOS host can be excluded from the tailnet for failing tailnet-lock checks, which the agent can detect from status JSON
scope_conditions: ipnstate TailnetLockStatus, added v1.102.0 (aliases of deprecated NetworkLockStatus from v1.30.0)

claim: Self-update progress is a distinct status surface (SelfUpdateStatus with UpdateFinished/UpdateInProgress/UpdateFailed and UpdateProgress{Status, Message, Version}), relevant to fleets where the tailscale client version itself is pinned by the OS (e.g. NixOS) and the CLI's --json version surfaces drift.
stance_target: fleet agent version-drift monitoring for the tailscale client
